description: A student in Japan wants to switch from Architecture to Digital Media. This creates a conflict: their current visa is tied to the specific faculty, and their credits may not transfer. They need to navigate the immigration and academic policy collision.

user_profile.persona: 20-year-old sophomore, creative but overwhelmed by bureaucracy
user_profile.context: Realized their passion lies elsewhere, but fears deportation or restarting from year one

fact_sheet.fact: The student, Kenji Tanaka, is enrolled at the Kyoto Institute of Global Arts (KIGA) with student ID 8945-2023.
Kenji is a second-year (sophomore) student in the Faculty of Urban Design, majoring in Architecture.
He wishes to transfer to the Faculty of Creative Informatics to major in Digital Media.
The internal application deadline for a faculty change for the Spring 2025 semester is November 15, 2024.
The "Internal Faculty Transfer Application" must be submitted through the KIGA-CampusWeb portal at https://campusweb.kiga.ac.jp.
A digital portfolio consisting of 5 to 8 creative works is a mandatory submission for the Digital Media program application.
A maximum of 12 credits from the Architecture curriculum are transferable to the Digital Media curriculum.
Kenji has completed 36 credits, of which only his 'UD205: History of Modern Architecture' course will count as a general arts elective.
His 'UD101: Principles of Structural Design' course (4 credits) is not transferable and will not count towards the new degree.
His current academic advisor is Professor Ito Hamada, whose office is in Building C, Room 402.
The Program Director for Digital Media, who must approve the transfer, is Dr. Akemi Sato.
Kenji's current Status of Residence is "Student" (留学), which is valid until April 30, 2026.
His visa is specifically linked to his enrollment in the "Faculty of Urban Design" at KIGA.
Changing faculties requires filing an "Application for Change of Status of Residence" with the immigration authorities.
The official form required for the visa status change is Form EX-03, downloadable from the Immigration Services Agency of Japan website.
The application must be submitted in person at the Kansai Regional Immigration Services Bureau, Kyoto Branch.
The immigration application requires an official "Letter of Acceptance" into the Faculty of Creative Informatics from KIGA.
A new Certificate of Enrollment (在学証明書) reflecting the Digital Media major must be obtained from the KIGA registrar's office for ¥300.
Proof of financial stability, such as a bank statement showing a balance of at least ¥1,500,000, is required for the visa application.
The standard government processing fee for a Change of Status of Residence application is ¥4,000, payable via a revenue stamp.
The KIGA International Student Center (ISC) provides guidance on immigration procedures and is located in the Student Union Building, 2nd Floor.
Ms. Yui Nakamura is the designated immigration advisor at the ISC; her direct email is y.nakamura@support.kiga.ac.jp.
Appointments with Ms. Nakamura can be booked through the "KIGA-LifeSupport" online system, with slots available on Tuesdays and Thursdays from 10:00 to 16:00.
Kenji must continue attending all his Architecture classes until both the faculty transfer and the visa change have been officially approved.
The annual tuition for the Faculty of Urban Design is ¥1,200,000.
The annual tuition for the Faculty of Creative Informatics is ¥1,350,000, an increase of ¥150,000 per year.
Kenji currently holds the "KIGA Global Leaders Scholarship," which provides a stipend of ¥50,000 per month.
The "KIGA Global Leaders Scholarship" is exclusively for students in the Faculty of Urban Design and will be terminated upon his transfer.
He can apply for the "Creative Futures Grant," a separate scholarship for Digital Media students, by the deadline of January 31, 2025.
Kenji resides in the KIGA-managed Sakura Dormitory, Room 305.
His housing contract is contingent on full-time student status at KIGA, not on his specific faculty, so his dorm room is secure.
For Kenji's faculty transfer case, the immigration step required after KIGA approves the move into Digital Media is to file an 'Application for Change of Status of Residence'.

For the KIGA-issued documents in this immigration filing, the university specifies two required supporting items: the Letter of Acceptance into the Faculty of Creative Informatics and the updated Certificate of Enrollment showing the Digital Media major.

user_needs.description: What is the deadline and submission portal for an internal faculty transfer application for Spring 2025?
How many creative works are required in the digital portfolio for the Digital Media program application?

user_needs.description: Because my student status is tied to the Faculty of Urban Design, do I need to file any immigration application for the transfer? If so, which one?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Once the user understands the academic application process, the most critical and stressful uncertainty is the impact on their visa status, making it a highly predictable next concern.

user_needs.description: What is the official form required for the visa status change and where can I download it?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After learning that an 'Application for Change of Status of Residence' is required, the user's immediate need is to identify and locate the specific form.

user_needs.description: Which KIGA-issued supporting documents are explicitly required for the immigration application?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying the government form, the user will need to know what supporting documents the university must provide for that application.

user_needs.description: What is the government fee for the visa application and what is the required proof of financial stability?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Once the user has a list of required documents, the associated costs and financial proofs are a natural follow-up question.
